# GeoGaussian
## Overview
GeoGaussian is a training modification for 3D Gaussian Splatting that improves geometric consistency by densifying new primitives on the tangent planes of existing Gaussians and encouraging smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring Gaussians [S1][S2, unofficial]. It addresses the irregular distribution and geometric discontinuities common in standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by constraining densification to local tangent surfaces [S1][S2, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) (which allows negative color values), [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md) (which constrains positions to a structured grid), [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md) (which replaces the kernel function), and [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md) (which injects blur kernels) by explicitly modifying the densification placement and adding geometric smoothness regularization [S1][S2, unofficial].
## How it works
**Inputs:** Current set of 3D Gaussians and training images. Not given in the sources for exact I/O specification.
**Outputs:** Updated set of 3D Gaussians. Not given in the sources.
**Data Structures:** Each Gaussian $i$ stores its position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$ [Parent]. Not given in the sources for additional structures.
**Steps:**
1. **Tangent Plane Densification:** When a Gaussian $i$ requires densification, new Gaussians are placed on the tangent plane of the parent Gaussian $i$ [S1][S2, unofficial].
2. **Geometric Smoothness Regularization:** A regularization term is added to the loss function to encourage smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring Gaussians [S1][S2, unofficial].
**Formulas:** Not given in the sources.
**Parameters:** Densification threshold, smoothness weight, and neighbor definition: Not given in the sources.
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:** Not given in the sources.
## Subtopics

### [Spatio-temporal Gaussian Tracking](9773-spatio-temporal-gaussian-tracking.md)
Spatio-temporal Gaussian Tracking (SGT) is a method for modeling surface dynamics in dynamic scenes by tracking the attribute shift of each Gaussian at time $t$ using a deformation field $D(\mu, t)$, allowing the rendering of deformed Gaussians $G_t$. It sets itself apart from static representations by explicitly parameterizing temporal deformation through a lightweight, decomposed encoding voxel and a set of small MLPs, prioritizing real-time inference speed over large neural network approximations. When to choose it: Not given in the sources.

### [Progressive training by scales of Gaussians](9871-progressive-training-by-scales-of-gaussians.md)
This method prevents rendering artifacts caused by 3D Gaussians becoming smaller than a single pixel during optimization by enforcing a minimum projected area through covariance regularization. It differs from standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by introducing a scale-dependent low-pass filter that focuses training on low-frequency details in early stages, ensuring coarse scene structure is learned efficiently before fine details are resolved. When to choose it: Not given in the sources.

Measured performance with its hardware, resolution and scene: Not given in the sources.
Scaling: Not given in the sources.
Strengths and limitations: Improves geometric consistency and smoothness of the reconstructed surface [S1][S2, unofficial]. May introduce additional computational overhead due to neighbor search and smoothness regularization [G].
When to use it and when not: Use when geometric accuracy and surface smoothness are prioritized over raw rendering speed or simplicity [S1][S2, unofficial]. Not given in the sources for when not to use.
## Background
Origin: Introduced in the survey "Recent advances in 3D Gaussian splatting" [S1][S2, unofficial].
History and development: It is part of the recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting that focus on improving the geometric properties of the representation [S1][S2, unofficial]. It builds on the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting framework [Parent].
Where it is used: Used in applications requiring high-quality geometric reconstruction from multi-view images [S1][S2, unofficial].
